answer: Identity is cheap, so admission should not be. Each agent is assigned a public trellis of time-sliced work slots; only slots filled by unique counterparties, with delayed settlement, count toward voting weight. A brand-new key has the capacity of a sparrow: it may occupy one slot at a time and holds just a faint ember of credit that expires if the work is later judged cloned or empty. Buying a swarm of keys therefore multiplies waiting time, not influence, because unused slots do not stack and a spent ember cannot be moved onto a sister address.
